title: Confounding Variables in Risk Data
text: Simpson’s paradox occurs trend appears aggregated data reverses disappears data split confounding variable. Risk data especially vulnerable : Exposure varies subgroup: everyone faces hazard equally Susceptibility varies subgroup: Age, genetics, occupation change vulnerability Reporting conflates subgroups: single “micromorts per year” figure averages across vastly different populations result: population-average micromort value may describe nobody accurately.

what: 2. Flagship Example: Bed Falls (Age as Confounder)
title: Confounding Variables in Risk Data
text: Falling bed kills ~450 Americans per year (CPSC). population average 1.36 micromorts/year. age massive confounder — CDC age-stratified data reveals 2,500-fold difference: 85-year-old man, going bed carries ~10 micromorts — comparable : Riding motorcycle 60 miles (10 micromorts/trip) single ecstasy dose (13 micromorts/dose) day skiing (0.7 micromorts/day) repeated 14 times someone 65, activity carries 0.004 micromorts per night — essentially zero. population average 1.36/year describes neither group accurately. Age confounds bed fall risk two pathways: Fragility: Older adults lower bone density, slower reflexes, higher complication rates identical falls Bed type environment: Hospital beds, care home beds, medication-induced drowsiness increase fall frequency older populations Neither pathway captured aggregate statistic.

title: Confounding Variables in Risk Data
text: confounding variable must satisfy two conditions: Correlated exposure: confounder determines exposed (e.g., farmers exposed cattle; office workers ) Correlated outcome: confounder affects probability death given exposure (e.g., age affects fall mortality; allergy affects sting mortality) encounter population-average risk: Ask “conditional ?” — identify likely confounders (age, sex, occupation, geography, pre-existing conditions) Seek stratified data — government agencies (CDC, CPSC, NOAA) often publish age- sex-stratified breakdowns Calculate conditional rates — use conditional_risk() package compare hedged vs unhedged scenarios Report range, average — range like “0.004–10.2 micromorts/night depending age” informative “1.36 micromorts/year”

what: 6. Geography of Disease: How Country Reshuffles Daily Risk
title: Confounding Variables in Risk Data
text: leading causes death vary dramatically country — just infectious diseases. Using IHME Global Burden Disease 2023 age-standardised death rates, can express chronic disease mortality daily micromorts. Key findings: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) leading killer everywhere, 3.24 mm/day UK 7.65 mm/day India (2.4x ratio). context, single skydive 8 mm — less 3 days background CVD risk India. Diarrheal diseases show starkest gap: 0.02 mm/day UK vs 1.28 mm/day India — 64x difference driven clean water sanitation infrastructure. Cancer higher UK (3.95 mm/day) India (2.3 mm/day) — counterintuitive finding. OWID data insight notes, richer countries avoid infectious chronic disease deaths, cancer exception age structure screening detection inflate high-income rates. Switching UK Nigeria profile reveals chronic diseases dominate daily risk far acute activity, gap countries structural — individual behaviour.

title: Introduction to Micromorts and Risk Visualization
text: Micromorts (acute, per-event risk) microlives (chronic, per-day attrition) measure different phenomena, can approximately converted using expected value theory. Key relationship: 1 micromort ≈ 0.7 microlives Assumptions conversion: 1. Remaining life expectancy = 40 years (use lle(prob, life_expectancy = ...) adjust age; see also daily_hazard_rate()) 2. Death occurs immediately upon event (worst case) 3. Linear approximation (valid small probabilities) Mathematical derivation: 1 micromort = 1/1,000,000 probability death Expected life lost = probability × remaining life = 1e-6 × 40 years = 4e-5 years = 4e-5 × 525,960 minutes/year ≈ 21 minutes 1 microlife = 30 minutes, 21 minutes ≈ 0.7 microlives common_risks() uses microlives = micromorts × 0.7: conversion allows comparing single risky event (like one skydive 8 micromorts) chronic daily habits (like smoking -10 microlives/day). However, approximation breaks : Remaining life expectancy differs 40 years (20-year-old loses per micromort 80-year-old) risk immediate death (injuries, disabilities captured) Repeated exposures compound non-linearly Use micromorts discrete, short-duration events binary outcomes (death survival): surgery, skydiving, single car trip Use microlives chronic, daily habits accumulate lifetime: smoking, exercise, diet Convert policy decisions, state assumptions (age, remaining life expectancy)

what: 6. Complementary Metrics: QALY, DALY, and Morbidity
title: Introduction to Micromorts and Risk Visualization
text: Micromorts microlives focus mortality. many conditions (like common cold) cause significant quality life loss without fatal. Complementary metrics capture morbidity burden. Measures years life adjusted quality. 1 QALY = 1 year perfect health. See NICE Methods Guide QALYs used health technology assessment. Health states weighted 0 (death) 1 (perfect health) year chronic pain 0.7 quality = 0.7 QALYs Used assess cost-effectiveness medical interventions (e.g., £20,000-30,000 per QALY threshold UK) Measured using instruments like EQ-5D (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain, anxiety) Measures disease burden sum two components. Defined Global Burden Disease study. YLL (Years Life Lost): premature mortality YLD (Years Lived Disability): morbidity, weighted disability weights fatal diseases like COVID-19, YLL dominates. non-fatal conditions like common cold, YLD dominates. Many widely-cited risk figures fail test: unknown denominators (many bee sting exposures per year?), misleading population averages (bed falls: 0.004 mm/night -65 vs 10.2 mm/night age 85+ male), fabricated numerators (“150 coconut deaths/year” myth). full treatment — denominator failures, inclusion criteria, cross-validation methods, worked examples — see Data Reliability vignette. confounding variables (age, geography, health profile) reshape risk rankings, see Confounding Variables.

title: Introduction to Micromorts and Risk Visualization
text: people fear flying (0.05 micromorts per flight) driving airport (1–3 micromorts)? David Ropeik’s Risk: Practical Guide Deciding ’s Really Safe ’s Really Dangerous (2002) identifies set psychological factors systematically distort risk perception away statistical reality. Ropeik’s key factors: Dread: Risks evoke vivid suffering (cancer, plane crashes) feel larger equivalent-mortality risks kill quietly (heart disease, falls) Control: Voluntary risks (skiing, smoking) feel smaller imposed risks (pollution, food additives) even equal micromort levels Familiarity: Novel risks (vaping, CRISPR) trigger fear longstanding ones (alcohol, driving) regardless evidence Catastrophic potential: single event killing 200 people generates fear 200 separate events killing one person, though mortality identical factors explain persistent pattern package’s data: activities people worry rarely ones highest micromort counts. Consider cancer example cancer_risks(): cancer accounts roughly 25% UK deaths, yet surveys consistently rank feared cause death — ahead cardiovascular disease, kills people (Ropeik 2010). chronic_disease_risks() data confirms cardiovascular daily micromorts exceed cancer daily micromorts every country dataset.

title: Introduction to Micromorts and Risk Visualization
text: practical goal micromort package help calibrate intuition evidence. Ropeik’s framework suggests three strategies: Anchor familiar risks. evaluating new risk, compare something already accept. quiz vignettes exactly — presenting pairs like “one skydive vs. 2.5 days UK cardiovascular risk” build intuitive anchors. Separate frequency dread. risk feels terrifying (shark attack: 0.001 micromorts/beach visit) may statistically negligible compared risk feels mundane (driving: 0.3 micromorts per 100 km). atomic_risks() function puts scale. Account chronic accumulation. Ropeik emphasises people consistently underestimate slow, cumulative risks relative dramatic one-events. combined_quiz_pairs() function designed make comparison explicit: one acute micromort event vs. equivalent number days chronic exposure. reading, see Slovic’s Perception Risk (2000) Fischhoff et al.’s foundational psychometric work (1978), provide empirical basis Ropeik’s framework.

what: 1. The Core Philosophy: Compare Apples to Oranges
title: Palatable Units: The Spiegelhalter Philosophy
text: goal palatable units create common currency risk. allows us strip away emotional “dread factor” scary-sounding events compare rationally mundane activities. Micromort: 1---million chance acute death (sudden event). Microlife: 30 minutes life expectancy lost/gained per day (chronic attrition). Abstract probabilities hard grasp. Spiegelhalter offers concrete anchor (Norm Chronicles, 2013; plus.maths.org): Flip fair coin 20 times. probability getting 20 heads row 1 1,048,576 — approximately 1 micromort. mathematical constant (1/2201/2^{20}), estimate. requires denominator, external source, geographic adjustment. can imagine surprise 20 consecutive heads, can feel scale 1 micromort. context, Gigerenzer (Calculated Risks, 2002) recommends expressing probabilities natural frequencies — counts defined population rather percentages. “1 death per 1,000,000 exposures” clearer “0.0001% mortality rate.” package follows convention: every micromort value traceable numerator (deaths) denominator (exposures).

title: Palatable Units: The Spiegelhalter Philosophy
text: micromort measures acute hazard: immediate probability event causing death. Normalization: Risk normalized per event (per unit distance), independent event’s duration. Skydiving: risk ~7 micromorts per jump. Whether freefall lasts 30 seconds 60 seconds secondary event jumping. Scuba Diving: risk ~5 micromorts per dive. 30-minute dive 45-minute dive treated single “dive events” broad statistics, though technically longer exposure increases risk. Anesthesia: ~10 micromorts per operation. following table uses common_risks(), package’s curated dataset 62 acute risks full provenance tracking: Comparison: Riding motorcycle just 60 miles carries acute death risk (~10 micromorts) undergoing general anesthesia. Using standardized dataset enables apples--apples comparisons across activities.

title: Palatable Units: The Spiegelhalter Philosophy
text: micromorts measure sudden death (Hazard), Microlives measure chronic attrition: rate “using ” life expectancy. Definition: 1 Microlife = 30 minutes life expectancy per day. Normalization: Risk normalized per day maintaining habit. Unit Attrition: “unit” expected lifespan. -1 Microlife means expected lifespan shrunk 30 minutes. Time Horizon: Continuous. smoke 20 cigarettes day, losing 10 microlives (5 hours) every single day. Using chronic_risks(), package’s curated dataset 22 chronic lifestyle factors: Clarification: value -1 Microlife loss (attrition). effectively means aging 30 minutes faster normal. annual_effect_days column shows cumulative impact year—-1 daily deficit sums ~7.5 days lost life annually.

title: Palatable Units: The Spiegelhalter Philosophy
text: Spiegelhalter advocates Logarithmic Risk Ladder. visualization helps placing rare risks (like asteroid impacts terrorism) context daily risks. Log Scale? risks span vast orders magnitude (1 10 1 10 million). Interpretation: “100% increase” rare risk (e.g., eating bacon increasing bowel cancer risk) might look huge headlines often negligible ladder compared baseline risk driving.  Spiegelhalter’s logarithmic risk ladder placing activities negligible (banana dose) extreme (BASE jumping) unified scale. interactive exploration, use plot_risks_interactive() provides: Hover details showing micromorts, microlives, period Click legend show/hide categories Dropdown filter COVID-19 vs risks Interactive risk ladder hover details, category filtering, zoom.

title: Palatable Units: The Spiegelhalter Philosophy
text: key motivation palatable units correcting perception gap fear actually kills us. According World Data, media coverage dramatically misrepresents actual causes death: Key insight: Heart disease cancer cause 56% deaths receive 7% media coverage. Meanwhile, terrorism (causing 16 deaths 2023) received 18,000× coverage proportional death rate. Micromorts microlives provide standardized currency cut emotional reactions: Terrorism (flying 2001): ~0.01 micromorts per flight Daily baseline (age 40): ~2 micromorts per day Driving 230 miles: 1 micromort fear flying 9/11 led many Americans drive instead, resulting estimated 1,600 additional road deaths—far exceeding attack’s direct toll. news reports “50% increase cancer risk,” use framework: Find baseline: ’s absolute risk? (e.g., 1 10,000) Convert micromorts: 1 10,000 = 100 micromorts Apply increase: 50% = 150 micromorts Compare familiar risks: 150 micromorts ≈ driving 150 × 230 = 34,500 miles contextualization reveals whether “scary” headline represents meaningful risk change.

title: Regional Variation in Life Expectancy
text: row represents aggregated population statistics one region-year-sex combination, individual survey responses. underlying Eurostat data represents ~400 million people across Western Europe. Life expectancy calculated official death registrations census population counts—sample survey. Row count formula: regions × years × 3 sex categories Sample data: 11 regions × 28 years × 3 = 924 rows Full dataset: 450 regions × 28 years × 3 = 37,800 rows

title: Regional Variation in Life Expectancy
text: Since mid-2000s, Western Europe fragmented : - Vanguard regions: Continued progress (~2.5 months/year gain men) - Laggard regions: Stalled improvement (<0.5 months/year gain) divergence reversed decades convergence observed 1990s.

title: Regional Variation in Life Expectancy
text: ~7 year gap vanguard laggard regions translates substantial lifetime difference microlives: 2.6 years LE gap = 45,496 lifetime microlives = 3.1 microlives/day Interpretation: Living vanguard region vs laggard region corresponds ~3.1 microlives per day—roughly equivalent benefit 30 minutes daily exercise.

title: Regional Variation in Life Expectancy
text: Data period: 2019 (pre-COVID baseline year, last year pandemic distortions) Column definitions: Key findings: Vanguard-laggard gap: ~7 years LE difference = ~8.4 microlives/day (equivalent 30 min daily exercise) Gap trend: Widened ~5 years (1992) ~7 years (2019) laggard regions stagnated post-2005 Top region: Comunidad de Madrid (ES) 86.1 years Bottom region: Mayotte (FR overseas) 74.9 years Microlives interpretation: +1.0 microlives/day ≈ +30 min life expectancy/day ≈ +7.6 days/year

title: REST API
text: Launch API R: interactive Swagger UI /__docs__/ lets explore endpoints, view parameter descriptions, try requests directly browser.
code: library(micromort) launch_api() #> ── Micromort Data API ── #> ℹ Starting server at http://127.0.0.1:8080 #> ℹ Swagger docs: http://127.0.0.1:8080/__docs__/

title: REST API
text: Every endpoint returns standard JSON envelope: data field contains result (array object). meta field includes package version, endpoint path, row count, ISO 8601 timestamp, query parameters used.
code: {   "data": [ ... ],   "meta": {     "source": "micromort v0.4.0",     "endpoint": "/v1/risks/acute",     "n_rows": 10,     "timestamp": "2026-03-09T12:00:00Z",     "params": { "category": "Medical" }   } }

title: REST API
text: Retrieve enriched acute risk data optional filtering category, minimum micromort threshold, result limit. Query chronic lifestyle factors gain lose microlives per day. Cancer mortality type, sex, age group family history multipliers.

title: REST API
text: Convert probability, micromorts, microlives, loss life expectancy.
code: # Probability to micromorts curl "http://localhost:8080/v1/convert/to-micromort?prob=0.000001"  # Micromorts to probability curl "http://localhost:8080/v1/convert/to-probability?micromorts=1"  # Loss of life expectancy (minutes) curl "http://localhost:8080/v1/convert/lle?prob=0.00001&life_expectancy=40"  # Monetary value of a micromort (default VSL = $10M) curl "http://localhost:8080/v1/convert/value?vsl=10000000" show_target("vig_api_conversion_table")

title: Risk Equivalence Dashboard
text: Atomic vs composite risks. atomic_risks() function returns ONE row per risk component per activity. Activities yet decomposed use component = "all_causes" (honest placeholder indicating breakdown unknown). Conditional risks. components depend health profile (e.g., DVT risk varies whether risk factors). default profile assumes “healthy” values; use common_risks(profile = list(health_profile = "dvt_risk_factors")) alternatives. Geographic conditioning can change equivalences dramatically: snake bite 0.5 mm US 18.5 mm rural Africa (37x). See Data Reliability vignette details. Duration bucketing. Rather encoding rate functions, flight risks pre-computed standard duration buckets (2h, 5h, 8h, 12h). Every number directly citable — hidden formulas. DVT literature. DVT risk 4 hours negligible. 4 hours, risk rises nonlinearly. Compression socks + hydration + movement reduce DVT risk approximately 60–70%. Sources: Lancet Haematology, Cochrane Reviews. Medical radiation. “(radiation)” label indicates radiation dose risk. invasive procedures (e.g., coronary angiogram), procedural risks (infection, bleeding) separate components yet decomposed. Confidence levels. component carries confidence rating: “high” (published meta-analyses), “medium” (single studies expert consensus), “low” (extrapolated), “estimated” (order--magnitude).

title: What is a Micromort?
text: Every morning involves risk. Brewing coffee. Crossing road. Commuting work. activity carries measurable probability death. micromort (mm) one---million chance death single activity. 1 mm — risks small never perceive dangerous. 12x ratio 30-minute bicycle commute cup coffee sounds alarming, absolute terms difference 0.01 0.12 million chance. negligible. Hover bars compare.

title: What is a Micromort?
text: Now zoom . Hover dot see activity name micromort value. micromort scale spans six orders magnitude — dental X-ray (0.05 mm) summiting Everest (~38,000 mm). Bottom (< 1 mm): daily activities — commuting, coffee, office work, dental X-rays. Risks small never notice . Middle (1–100 mm): risks weigh consciously — night hospital (75 mm), general anaesthesia (10 mm), long-haul flight (4 mm), running marathon (7 mm). Top (> 100 mm): risks make headlines — base jumping (430 mm per jump), Himalayan mountaineering (12,000 mm), Everest ~38,000 mm — roughly 4% chance death per ascent.

title: What is a Micromort?
text: risks kill instant. shorten life half hour, every single day. David Spiegelhalter called microlives (ml) — one worth 30 minutes life expectancy. Smoking 20 cigarettes day costs 10 microlives. 10 × 30 = 300 minutes = 5 hours life, lost every 24 hours. heavy smoker lives though day 19 hours long. scale works reverse . 150 minutes weekly exercise gains 3 ml/day. Five servings fruit vegetables: +4 ml/day — yes, diet can outweigh exercise Spiegelhalter’s estimates (BMJ 2012 paper). Mediterranean diet: +2 ml/day. Hover bars explore. Red = life lost. Green = life gained.

title: What is a Micromort?
text: compare skydive cigarette? One kills instantly (rarely). kills slowly (certainly, scale). answer Loss Life Expectancy (LLE) — average time lost gained per exposure. One micromort costs roughly 21 minutes life expectancy. One microlife 30 minutes. 1 mm ≈ 0.7 ml. UK Department Transport values micromort £1.60. NICE values microlife £1.70. Two independent government agencies, nearly price unit risk. three currencies risk exchange rate .

title: Microlives per Micromort Conversion Factor — MICROLIVES_PER_MICROMORT
text: 1 micromort = 1--1,000,000 (1e-6) probability death specific acute exposure. 1 microlife = 30 minutes life expectancy.

title: Microlives per Micromort Conversion Factor — MICROLIVES_PER_MICROMORT
text: Following life-expectancy framework introduced Spiegelhalter (2012), micromort's expected cost life expectancy ("loss life expectancy", LLE) exposure probability multiplied life expectancy remaining time exposure. package follows common convention (matching derivation already used internally combined_quiz_pairs()) assuming 40 years remaining life expectancy "average" adult:   .e. MICROLIVES_PER_MICROMORT = (40 * 365 * 24 * 60 * 1e-6) / 30, evaluates 0.7008 stored rounded one decimal place 0.7.
code: LLE_minutes  = 1e-6 * 40 years * 365 days/year * 24 hours/day * 60 min/hour              = 1e-6 * 21,024,000 minutes              = 21.024 minutes microlives   = LLE_minutes / 30 minutes-per-microlife              = 21.024 / 30              = 0.7008 -> rounds to 0.7

title: Microlives per Micromort Conversion Factor — MICROLIVES_PER_MICROMORT
text: 40-year remaining-life-expectancy assumption simplification: true conversion factor varies age (micromort taken late life converts fewer microlives one taken early life, less remaining life expectancy lose). 0.7 therefore population-average approximation, individually-calibrated value. package able trace exact 0.7 figure verbatim formula Spiegelhalter's original BMJ paper (derivation package's reconstruction, cross-checked independent secondary sources report 40-year assumption arithmetic); general micromort/microlife framework , however, directly attributable paper.

title: Convert Minutes to Microlives — as_microlife
text: minutes Numeric. Life expectancy change minutes. Positive values = life gained (e.g., exercise) Negative values = life lost (e.g., smoking) use_units Logical. TRUE, returns units object unit "microlife". Default FALSE returns plain numeric backwards compatibility.

title: Convert Minutes to Microlives — as_microlife
text: Numeric. Value microlives (sign input), units object use_units = TRUE.

title: Convert Minutes to Microlives — as_microlife
text: Unit definition: 1 microlife = 30 minutes life expectancy change per day. Sign convention: Negative microlives = life expectancy loss (harmful) Positive microlives = life expectancy gain (beneficial)

title: Convert Minutes to Microlives — as_microlife

what: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
title: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
text: Creates candidate question pairs mixing acute risks common_risks() (micromorts per event) chronic risks chronic_risks() (microlives per day), converting common microlife scale can directly compared. pair pits one acute activity one chronic lifestyle factor asks larger total impact time_period_days.

title: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
code: combined_quiz_pairs(n = 10, time_period_days = 365, seed = NULL)

title: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
text: n Integer. Number pairs generate. Default 10. time_period_days Numeric. Time period chronic risk accumulation. Default 365 (1 year). chronic risks, cumulative impact abs(microlives_per_day) × time_period_days. seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. Default NULL (random call). Acute risks period_type == "event" (true one-events one expedition one base jump) keep raw micromort value. Acute risks period type day/hour/month/year represent repeatable rate exposure projected time_period_days via micromorts_per_day_raw × time_period_days conversion microlives. period_type == "period" rows split period string: plain "N weeks (YEAR)" surveillance-rate phrasing (e.g. "11 weeks (2022)") scales day/hour/month/year, "per N weeks"/"per N months" bounded-window phrasing (e.g. "per 8 weeks" specific historical interval) keeps raw micromort value like event row. unrounded column (micromorts_per_day_raw) used rather display-rounded micromorts_per_day prevent low-rate annual/monthly rows collapsing zero rounding (e.g. 0.003 µm/day rounds 0.00).

title: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
text: tibble columns: activity_a, type_a ("acute"), value_a (raw micromorts stored), unit_a ("micromorts"), category_a, period_a, period_type_a (one "event", "day", "hour", "month", "year", "period"), effective_micromorts_a (raw value "event" rows bounded-window "period" rows; micromorts_per_day_raw × time_period_days otherwise) factor_b, type_b ("chronic"), value_b, unit_b ("microlives/day"), category_b, direction_b common_unit ("microlives"), common_value_a (effective_micromorts_a × 0.7), common_value_b correct_answer ("" "b" — whichever higher impact common unit) ratio (larger / smaller common value) explanation describing values conversion

title: Generate cross-domain quiz pairs comparing acute and chronic risks — combined_quiz_pairs
text: conversion micromorts microlives uses factor 0.7 (1 micromort ≈ 0.7 microlives age 40). Chronic impact time period abs(microlives_per_day) × time_period_days.

title: Acute Risks in Micromorts — common_risks
text: profile named list condition variables filtering conditional risks, e.g. list(health_profile = "dvt_risk_factors") list(country = "US") country-specific road traffic homicide risks. Default list() returns unconditional/healthy defaults. duration_hours Optional numeric. duration-dependent activities, selects nearest pre-computed duration bucket within activity. flying variants (2h, 5h, 8h, 12h) retained. NULL (default) returns duration buckets. Use risk_for_duration() select single activity family result.

Suitable display; may collapse 0.00 low-rate rows (e.g. annual risk / 365). Use micromorts_per_day_raw downstream computation. micromorts_per_day_raw Unrounded micromorts per day (micromorts / period_days). what: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
text: Calculates daily probability death based age using simplified Gompertz-Makeham mortality model. Returns central estimate plus credible bounds derived ±10% sensitivity Gompertz parameters (background mortality) b (initial mortality).

title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
code: daily_hazard_rate(age, sex = "male")

title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
text: age Age years sex "male" "female" (default: "male")

title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
text: tibble : age Input age sex Input sex daily_prob Daily probability death (central estimate) micromorts Daily baseline risk micromorts (central estimate) micromorts_lower Lower credible bound (micromorts) ±10% parameter sensitivity micromorts_upper Upper credible bound (micromorts) ±10% parameter sensitivity microlives_consumed Estimated microlives consumed per day precision_note Reminder Gompertz parameters approximate interpretation Human-readable summary

title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
text: Gompertz hazard h(x) = + b * exp(c * x). Bounds computed varying b independently ±10% (four combinations) taking min/max across combinations.

title: Daily Hazard Rate by Age — daily_hazard_rate
text: Gompertz B (1825). "Nature Function Expressive Law Human Mortality." Philosophical Transactions Royal Society.

title: Generate Quiz Pairs for
text: Creates candidate question pairs common_risks() use interactive risk comparison quiz. pair contains two activities similar micromort values, making comparison challenging educational.

title: Generate Quiz Pairs for
code: quiz_pairs(   min_ratio = 1.1,   max_ratio = 2,   prefer_cross_category = TRUE,   seed = NULL,   difficulty = NULL,   profile = list() )

title: Generate Quiz Pairs for
text: min_ratio Minimum ratio micromort values pair. Values 1.0 exclude identical-risk pairs unanswerable. Default 1.1. Ignored difficulty non-NULL. max_ratio Maximum ratio micromort values pair. Lower values produce harder questions. Default 2.0. Ignored difficulty non-NULL. prefer_cross_category TRUE (default), pairs different risk categories prioritised -category pairs. seed Optional random seed reproducibility. difficulty Optional difficulty level. One "easy", "medium", "hard", "mixed". non-NULL, overrides min_ratio max_ratio use full pool (ratios 1.5–10) assigns difficulty based data-driven terciles: hard: lowest third ratios (hardest distinguish) medium: middle third easy: highest third (easiest distinguish) mixed: samples equally three tiers NULL (default), original min_ratio/max_ratio behaviour preserved difficulty column added. profile named list condition variables filtering conditional risks, passed common_risks(). E.g. list(country = "US") include country-specific disease mortality quiz pool. Default list() uses population-average unconditional risks .

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: country Character vector. Filter specific countries using ISO 2-letter codes (e.g., "FR", "DE", "ES"). Default NULL returns countries. year Integer vector. Filter specific years. Default NULL returns years (1992-2023). sex Character. Filter sex: "Male", "Female", "Total". Default NULL returns . classification Character. Filter region classification: "vanguard", "average", "laggard". Default NULL returns .

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: tibble columns: region_code NUTS2 region code (e.g., "FR10" Île-de-France) region_name Human-readable region name country_code ISO 2-letter country code year Data year (1992-2023) sex Sex category: "Male", "Female", "Total" life_expectancy Life expectancy birth years microlives_vs_eu_avg Daily microlives difference vs EU average classification "vanguard", "average", "laggard" based 2019 trends source_url DOI link source publication

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: row represents one region-year-sex combination, individual survey responses. example, dataset 450 regions × 28 years × 3 sex categories = 37,800 rows aggregated statistics. underlying Eurostat data represents ~400 million people across Western Europe. Life expectancy calculated official death registrations census population counts—sample survey.

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: Primary data Eurostat dataset demo_r_mlifexp. Regional classifications based Bonnet et al. (2026) methodology identifying: Vanguard regions: Top 20% life expectancy sustained gains (≥1.5 months/year) Laggard regions: Bottom 20% life expectancy stagnant gains (<0.5 months/year) Average regions: others

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: microlives_vs_eu_avg column converts life expectancy differences daily microlives using approximation: 1 year LE difference ≈ 1.2 microlives/day (assuming 40 years remaining life expectancy). Example: region +2 years EU average = +2.4 microlives/day, equivalent benefit 20 minutes daily exercise.

title: Regional Life Expectancy in Western Europe — regional_life_expectancy
text: IMPORTANT: Regional life expectancy reflects population averages, individual-level causation. High life expectancy "vanguard" regions results multiple factors including: Healthcare system quality access Socioeconomic composition (income, education) Selection effects (healthy/wealthy people moving certain regions Historical cultural factors Moving high-LE region guarantee increased personal longevity.
